newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: EU deal "may lose S.Africa neighbours 1 bln rand".
newsitem.headline: EU deal "may lose S.Africa neighbours 1 bln rand".

text.p: South Africa's customs union neighbours -- Botswana, Lesotho, Namibia and Swaziland (BLNS) -- could lose more than one billion rand in crucial fiscal revenue if the proposed free trade accord between South African and the European Union was concluded, Business Day newspaper reported.
The figure was contained in a report done by a Zimbabwe-based research consultancy and financed by the EU, which has been kept secret, the paper said.

The report, which was co-ordinated by Swaziland, strengthens the case of South Africa's negotiators that the free trade area, as proposed by the EU in its mandate is not "developmental" and would harm BLNS nations which are heavily dependent on the revenue they receive from the cusoms union pool with South Africa.

South Africa is currently in negotiations with the EU on a free trade pact between the two areas. Negotiations have hit a number of stumbling blocks in recent months including Pretoria's opposition to the EU mandate's exclusion of almost 39 percent of South Africa's farm products.
South Africa's neighbours have also been outspoken about the potential negative effects a trade agreement could have on them.

Business Day said a number of sources on Monday disputed the accuracy of the one billion rand figure, with some saying it was too high and others too low. The EU is understood to have found problems with the preliminary findings of the report.
